components.css: .ds-stages{display:flex;border-top:1px solid var(--line)}.ds-stages button{display:flex;width:100%;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:6px;border:0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:0;padding:16px 4px;background:transparent;color:var(--text);font:13px Inter,sans-serif;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;transition:color 150ms,background-color 150ms}.ds-stages span{font:11px/1.7 'JetBrains Mono',monospace;letter-spacing:.025em;color:var(--muted)}.ds-stages button:hover,.ds-stages button[aria-pressed=true]{background:color-mix(in oklab,var(--accent) 10%,transparent)}.ds-stages button[aria-pressed=true]{color:var(--accent-readable)}.ds-stages button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent);outline-offset:4px}@media(min-width:768px){.ds-stages{display:block}.ds-stages button{justify-content:flex-start;gap:16px;padding:16px 12px;font-size:16px}.ds-stages span{letter-spacing:.075em}}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-stages button{transition:none}}

Let’s talk

Have an engineering opportunity?

narrative.northStar: Engineering field notebook crossed with an aircraft instrument panel
narrative.overview:
An aerospace engineering portfolio for recruiters, engineering teams, and collaborators. The visual language should feel technical, assured, and evidence-led: an editorial presentation built on drafting-grid structure, oversized typography, restrained color, and real project artifacts.

This direction is informed by the visual language of [herdr.dev](https://herdr.dev/). Following the owner's September 10, 2026 correction, use its live Ink/Paper palette: lavender on charcoal and violet on warm paper. This supersedes the earlier signal-orange direction. Retain Lee's approved identity-first, evidence-led composition; do not reproduce Herdr's branding, ram motif, terminal mock, or copy.
keyCharacteristics: Real engineering artifacts at natural proportions.
Square composition, hairline divisions, and theme-aware interaction feedback.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Use lavender in Ink and violet in Paper; preserve the same hierarchy across themes.

dos: Do preserve the Ink/Paper hierarchy and semantic theme bindings.
Do show real project evidence at its natural proportions.
Do keep contribution and limitations visible beside the work.
Do respect reduced motion and retain native disclosure behavior.
donts: Don't replace project artifacts with simulated CAD or terminal interfaces.
Don't crop away engineering details to force uniform thumbnail boxes.
